stem: A school-aged child with pneumonia has worsening respiratory distress. Which chest X-ray feature would most strongly support pleural effusion rather than atelectasis or collapse?

options.text: A lateral line of demarcation that can occupy much of the lung field
A triangular opacity with a uniform density
A sharply demarcated opacity with shift towards the consolidation
A broad upper mediastinum caused by a triangular sail-like opacity

explanation: Pleural effusion is the best answer because it can produce a lateral line of demarcation and may occupy much of the lung field on chest X-ray.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because pleural effusion can create a lateral line of demarcation and may obscure much of the lung field.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a triangular opacity with uniform density is more typical of atelectasis.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a sharply demarcated opacity with shift towards the consolidation is more consistent with collapse.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a rounded airspace change suggests round pneumonia rather than pleural effusion.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a triangular sail-like opacity in the upper mediastinum is the thymic sail sign, not pleural fluid.
